equity_bridge.item: H1-2026 owner FCF already reflected in 2026-06-30 net debt
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 FCF $532M less SBC $62M less equity-award withholding $54M; removed because year-1 (FY2026) flows are projected in full while net debt is struck mid-year

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.0-3.3%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (8-10%) and EPS (~25.5%). Book value is suppressed by ~$3.6B of buybacks FY2020-H1 2026 plus dividends, and still carries the 2019 GE Transportation goodwill; it does not measure the business's growth. Revenue 5-yr CAGR (8.1%, includes 2025-26 M&A) is used as the reference; EPS CAGR is flattered by margin expansion from a COVID-depressed FY2020 base and falling share count.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC expense less equity-award withholding; FY2020 withholding not in CSV, ~$5M assumed). Owner-FCF CAGR (17-18%) is ~1pp below reported (18-19%): SBC + withholding grew from ~$25M to $134M, faster than FCF, but remains ~1.2% of revenue -- immaterial to the thesis. FY2025 FCF ($1,499M) fell from FY2024 ($1,627M) on working-capital build and higher interest.

scenario_narratives.base: Wabtec delivers the raised FY2026 guide and converts its record $9.1B backlog at a mid-single-digit organic pace: North American Class I locomotive modernisation and new-unit orders hold up, international mining (Vale, BHP, FLXdrive) adds volume, and the aftermarket/LTSA annuity on 23,000+ locomotives grows with the aging fleet. Digital Intelligence and Dellner lift mix, so pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands from ~23% to 24.5% and stops there as tariff and input-cost pressure absorbs further pricing. Leverage (~2.2x net debt/EBITDA) deleverages from cash flow without needing equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: The freight equipment upcycle is real and long: carload traffic recovers, Class I railroads refresh aging fleets and step up modernisations, mining electrification orders scale, and Digital Intelligence keeps compounding at high rates, pushing organic growth to 7-9% for several years. Mix shift to services, software and safety-critical Dellner couplers plus productivity take EBITDA margin to ~26.5%, and tariff costs are fully passed through. The business earns a higher-quality, more recurring multiple (16x exit cap).
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 comes in slightly under guidance and a freight recession follows: Class I railroads -- a concentrated, powerful customer group -- cut capex and defer locomotive deliveries, revenue is flat in FY2027 and falls 3% in FY2028 as backlog conversion slips. Tariffs and steel/electronics inflation are only partly passed through, Dellner integration disappoints, and CRRC pressure on international transit tenders squeezes pricing, so EBITDA margin gives back ~2pp to 21% before recovering to 22%. The aftermarket base cushions but does not prevent the cycle; growth resumes at low single digits and the business re-rates to a cyclical 13x exit cap.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict house basis: SBC plus equity-award withholding expensed, share count flat, US GAAP operating leases inside EBITDA, NCI deducted once, net debt struck at the latest (Q2-2026) balance sheet with the H1-2026 flows removed so they are not counted twice. Wabtec's value rests on a sticky aftermarket annuity layered under a cyclical equipment book; the market price capitalises the current margin trajectory at a multiple well above what a 9% WACC with a 15x exit cap supports.
key_risks_to_valuation: Freight rail cycle: Class I capex cuts would hit new locomotive and modernisation orders with a 2-4 quarter lag
Customer concentration among a few North American Class I railroads
Tariff and input-cost inflation (steel, electronics, engines) eroding the margin expansion path
Leverage: gross debt $3.98B (FY2024) -> $6.57B (Q2-2026) after Dellner and 2025 acquisitions; refinancing of $1.66B current maturities at higher rates
M&A integration (Dellner, 2025 Evident/Frauscher deals) and the habit of buying growth
Terminal value dependence: most of value sits beyond year 5 at a 15x cap

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $94M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $40M (financing). Wabtec publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two are summed. The cash-flow add-back is $80M; the $94M expense basis is used for consistency with the Metrics.csv SBC series and is the more conservative. H1-2026: $62M expense + $54M withholding (Q1 vesting-heavy).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 $223M, FY2024 $1,097M, H1-2026 $457M (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock). Active repurchaser: the flat count is funded. Diluted weighted shares fell 179.5M (FY2023) -> 169.6M (Q2-2026).
inputs.projected_shares_note: Flat 169.6M: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so the count is not also diluted. No non-SBC issuance (Dellner and the 2025 acquisitions were cash/debt funded).
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares 169.6M (basic 169.1M shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 plus ~0.5M dilutive RSUs/PSUs/options). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed. Q3-2026 buybacks are not yet filed; any repurchase both lowers the count and raises net debt, roughly value-neutral near IV.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt $6,571M = XBRL LongTermDebt at 2026-06-30 (noncurrent $4,915M + current portion $1,656M). The Metrics.csv TotalDebt of $8,227M (and $6,791M FY2025) ADDS the current portion to LongTermDebt, which already includes it -- a double-count; the Analysis JSON's '~$8.2B' inherits that error. Cash $660M = cash, equivalents and restricted cash $670M less $10M restricted. Gross debt did rise sharply ($3,980M FY2024 -> $6,571M Q2-2026) to fund $2.5B of 2025 acquisitions (Evident inspection, Frauscher), the ~$1.06B Dellner purchase (Feb-2026) and buybacks; net debt / FY2025 EBITDA ~2.6x, ~2.2x on H1-2026 annualised. Operating lease liabilities ($365M) excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost already sits inside EBITDA (treatment B, no lease line needed).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (2025-26 issuance), ~3.9% after tax. Market weights: equity ~$48.8B, net debt ~$5.9B (~11%). WACC ~9.15%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: freight-cycle and customer-concentration risk are carried in the bear flows and its weight, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease expense is inside EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest $30M at 2026-06-30 (NCI share of NI $13M FY2025, ~1%) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated.
inputs.pension_note: Defined-benefit obligations are small relative to EV and not bridged; immaterial at this scale.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (engine build via make build-dcf). Wabtec is an operating industrial (freight locomotives/components/services/digital + transit equipment); routing table row 'Operating company, cyclical: industrials' -> owner-FCF + adaptations. Adaptations applied: USD WACC, single lease treatment (US GAAP operating leases in EBITDA), NCI once in the bridge, risk charged once (same WACC all scenarios). No SBC-zero collapse (US filer, SBC ~1.2% of revenue). FY0 = FY2025 (revenue $11,167M); year 1 = FY2026 anchored to raised guidance midpoint $12.45B. Because net debt is struck at 2026-06-30, the H1-2026 owner FCF already sits inside it; the equity bridge removes it once so year-1 flows are not counted twice. EBITDA margins in the drivers are GAAP EBITDA (operating income + D&A) with SBC ADDED BACK, because the engine deducts SBC separately: FY2025 = (2,294 + 94)/11,167 = 21.4%; H1-2026 = (1,399 + 62)/6,129 = 23.8%. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes paid $342M on pre-tax income $1,592M after ~$225M interest; unlevered (adding back the ~$50M interest shield) ~22% of EBIT. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventory + contract assets well above payables + contract liabilities -> NEGATIVE capture on revenue growth. No live corporate action; three-scenario frame applies.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the raised guidance midpoint ($12.45B, +11.5% incl. ~3pp Dellner/acquisitions and FX); growth then settles to mid-single-digit organic as the record $9.1B backlog converts and the aftermarket compounds, fading to 3% by year 10. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands ~1.5pp more as mix shifts to services and Digital Intelligence and Dellner integrates, then holds at 24.5%. D&A glides down as GE Transportation acquisition intangibles amortise off.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the stock sits near its 52-week high after a guidance raise, gross debt has risen ~65% in 18 months, and freight equipment demand is cyclical and concentrated in a handful of Class I railroads. Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice and the backlog is at a record, giving good 12-24 month visibility. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): the bull path needs a multi-year freight upcycle, sustained Digital Intelligence hypergrowth and full tariff pass-through to all go right together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
